 Oral Judgment
This appeal is filed against the judgment and award dated 02.11.2022 passed by the II Additional Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Kalaburagi, in MVC No.1284 of 2019.

entities.text: II Additional Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Kalaburagi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The claimant met with an accident on 10.09.2019 and sustained grievous injures.
Therefore, he filed a claim petition before the Tribunal, claiming compensation of Rs.31,00,000/-.

3. The Tribunal, considering the entire evidence on record, calculated total compensation of Rs.3,82,187/-, but as there was contributory negligence on the part of rider and driver of both the vehicles, it was held 50% NC: 2025:KHC-K:6767 HC-KAR negligence on the part of the appellant and fixed the remaining 50% liability on the owner and insurer of the truck and thereby awarded only 50% of the said amount i.e., Rs.1,91,094/- with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realisation and directed respondent No.2- Insurance Company to pay the said amount.

4. Aggrieved by the said judgment and award, the injured claimant has preferred this appeal,
disputing the quantum of compensation as well as liability, contending that, the Tribunal has awarded meagre amounts under relevant heads.
Though he was earning Rs.20,000/- per month, the Tribunal has taken his income only at Rs.13,250/- per month.
PW.2-Doctor assessed the disability at 21.04%, but the Tribunal instead of taking it as 10% has taken as only 3%.
Therefore, requested for enhancement of compensation.

entities.text: Santosh S/O Mallappa vs Mohammed Alam

sentences.text: Heard the arguments of both sides.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:6767 HC-KAR 6.
Though the appellant sated that he was earning Rs.20,000/- per month, he has not produced any income proof.
Therefore, the Tribunal has rightly taken his notional income at Rs.13,250/- per month as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, as the accident is of the year 2019.
He was aged 23 years and therefore, the multiplier was rightly taken as '18'.
Ex.P4 is the wound certificate and Exs.P7 and 8 are the discharge cards.

PW.2 issued the disability certificate under Ex.P10 and stated that, on examination of petitioner and clinical findings it was noted that,
Mandibular deviation, while opening and closing, on percussion of TMS Pt. experiences pain Maloceulusion noted, fracture of 1/3rd of lower front teeth noted i.e., 31, 32, 33, 41, 42 and 43 associated with pain on percussion.
Therefore, he assessed the disability at 21.04% and the other Doctor issued disability certificate under Ex.P9.

The Tribunal simply stated that, the disability assessed by the doctor is on the higher side and has taken 1/3rd of 10% i.e., 3% to the NC:
2025:KHC-K:6767 HC-KAR whole body, which should be enhanced to 1/3rd of 21% i.e., 7% instead of 3%.

Thus, the loss of future earnings would be:
Rs.13,250 x 12 x 18 x 7% = 2,00,340/-.
7.
The Tribunal has awarded an amount of Rs.1,89,827/- towards medical expenses as per the medical documents and it needs no interference.
8. The appellant was admitted in the hospital for 05 days.

Considering the nature of injuries and period of hospitalisation, this Court finds it reasonable to grant an amount of Rs.75,000/- for pain and suffering, Rs.25,000/- for loss of amenities and Rs.30,000/- for transportation, extra nourishment and attendant charges.
9. The appellant might not have attended any work at least for a period of three months due to the injuries sustained.

Therefore, this Court finds it reasonable to grant an amount of Rs.39,750/-
(Rs.13,250 x 3) for loss of income during laid up period.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:6767 HC-KAR 10.

Hence, the appellant is entitled for the modified compensation under different heads as below:
Pain and suffering Rs.75,000/-
Medical expenses Rs.1,89,827/-
Loss of future earnings Rs.2,00,340/-
Loss of income during laid up period Rs.39,750/- Transportation, extra nourishment, Rs.30,000/-
and attendant charges Loss of amenities Rs.25,000/-
Total Rs.5,59,917/-

3
Thus, the appellant is entitled for total compensation of Rs.5,59,917/- with interest at 6% per annum and therefore, the appeal deserves to be allowed in part.

11. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that, 50% of the negligence was fixed on the appellant,
in fact the entire liability is to be fixed on the respondent No.2, but there is no specific order or direction in the operative portion of the Judgment regarding that aspect.
12. On perusal of the Judgment, the claimant was returning to his village on motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-39/R-6542, at that time a lorry bearing registration NC: 2025:KHC-K:6767 HC-KAR No.TS-12/UC-3888 was parked on the road without following the traffic rules and regulations and without any indicators, as a result he dashed to the lorry.
Charge sheet is filed against both the drivers i.e. rider of the motorcycle and the driver of the lorry.
Considering the said fact, the tribunal has assessed the contributory negligence in the ratio of 50:50 on each of the vehicle drivers.

13. Section 15 of the Rules of the Road Regulations, 1989 reads as under:
15. Parking of the vehicle.-(l) Every driver of a motor vehicle parking on anyroad shall park in such a way that it does not cause or is not likely to cause danger or obstruction or undue inconvenience to other road users and.
the manner of parking is indicated by any sign board or markings on the road side, he shall park his vehicle in such manner.

Merely because the charge-sheet is filed against both the vehicles, it cannot be said that,
there is contributory negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle also.

15. Further, it is also forthcoming that, no reasons are assigned for parking the vehicle in the middle of the road in the national highway and the accident has NC: 2025:KHC-K:6767 HC-KAR occurred at 12.50 a.m. i.e. in the midnight.

Therefore, the accident has occurred only due to the negligence of the driver in parking the lorry and owner and the insurer of the lorry bearing registration No.TS-12/UC-3888 are liable to pay the compensation.
16. Therefore, respondent No.2-Insurance company is directed to deposit the entire compensation along with interest accrued on it, within one month from the date of this order.

17. In the result, the following order is passed:
 (i) Appeal is allowed in part.
( ii) The appellant/claimant is entitled for total compensation of Rs.5,59,917/- with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization.
(iii) Respondent No.2-Insurance Company is directed to deposit the aforesaid compensation amount within one month from the date of this judgment.
- 10 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:6767 HC-KAR (iv) On such deposit, the appellant is permitted to withdraw the entire amount along with interest accrued on it.
